transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
- Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Rylan Barton.
California Democratic Attorney General Rob Bonta
is suing OpenAI after one of its AI agents
hacked into another company this summer
from member station KQED, Ella Jackson reports.
- In July, OpenAI tested a new agentic model
that broke containment and hacked into Hugging Face,
another AI platform.
Without OpenAI's knowledge.
Bonta alleges that this violated
California's unfair competition law.
He says that OpenAI is responsible for its agents' actions
and that a lack of controls put everyone at risk.
- Without proper safeguards and monitoring,
these models pose a danger
to anything connected to the internet.
They can intrude into, degrade, or shut down
the services people rely on every day.
- A spokesperson for OpenAI says that it has been addressing
the "misaligned" model activity
and that the lawsuit singles out the company
for a challenge that every AI lab faces.
For NPR News, I'm Ella Jackson in San Francisco.
- JP Morgan Chase said it had suffered an outage
that affected customers at the country's
biggest lender today, but a spokesperson later said
transactions were back to normal.
NPR's Rafael Naam has the story.
- Chase blamed an incident on a software bug
and said it was not cyberrelated.
Earlier, some customers had complained
about being unable to use Chase ATMs
or conduct some online transactions.
The bug also affected other banks and their customers,
impacting things like money transfers
from Chase to other lenders.
The incident is the latest tech failure to hit the US.
Last week, Microsoft reported a major outage,
while the Federal Aviation Administration
set an issue with old equipment
led to widespread flight disruptions.
Also on Monday, United Airlines temporarily delayed
some flights after suffering its own system outage.
Rafael Naam, NPR News.
- Pope Leo is on his way back to Rome
after his trip through Latin America.
Millions greeted him along the way in Uruguay,
Argentina, and Peru to an emotional homecoming,
and PR's Kerry Khan reports.
- At his final mass of this visit,
Pope Leo said goodbye to Peru.
- Gracias, Peru!
(crowd cheering)
- He thanked the millions who flocked to see him
when he traveled from the coastal capital Lima
to the Andean city of Cusco some 11,000 feet high
and the Amazon city of Pulcalpa,
where he decried the killings of environmental defenders.
The blood of these brothers cries out to God
and demands justice, he said.
Despite having lung cancer surgery last month,
the Pope showed no fatigue in his visit
to three countries over 12 days.
Kerry Khan, NPR News.
- Major U.S. stock indexes fell today.
Nvidia led another sell-off in tech stocks
and helped drag the U.S. market lower.
The S&P 500 fell nearly 2%.
This is NPR News.
Leadership failures, lack of preparedness,
and poor communication were the driving factors
of a wildfire that destroyed a historic lodge
and dozens of structures at Grand Canyon National Park.
That's according to a federal review
of last year's Dragon Bravo fire,
while drought conditions and extreme fire behavior
were contributing factors,
the review highlights systemic weaknesses
in National Park Service fire leadership governance.
The handwritten draft of Dr. Martin Luther King Jr.'s 1963
"I Have a Dream" speech is now on display
at the National Center for Civil and Human Rights in Atlanta.
From member station WABE, Alex Helmic reports
it's set to be auctioned in January.
- Speechwriter Edward Clayton was one of those
who helped King with the speech
delivered from the steps of the Lincoln Memorial
on August 28th, 1963.
Clayton's wife, civil rights advocate Zernona Clayton,
discovered the handwritten draft in the '90s
in her late husband's desk,
tucked inside an envelope labeled "Speech."
It includes the opening lines and powerful finish,
but not the famous "I Have a Dream" refrain,
which King added spontaneously.
The draft will head to Chicago for viewing
and then to New York to be auctioned off at Christie's
where they estimate it could fetch more than $10 million.
Money from the sale will go to the Zernona Clayton Foundation
and the King Center in Atlanta.
For NPR News, I'm Alex Helmic in Atlanta.
- AAA says pricey plane tickets and gas
are expected to keep some Americans
from traveling for Thanksgiving,
but not enough to make much of a difference
in airport security lines and highway traffic.
This is NPR News from Washington.

topics.text: California AG Rob Bonta sues OpenAI after its AI agent hacked into Hugging Face in July
JP Morgan Chase outage hits ATMs and online transactions; company says bug, not cyberattack
Pope Leo returns to Rome after 12-day Latin America trip through Uruguay, Argentina, Peru
Major U.S. stock indexes fall as Nvidia leads tech sell-off; S&P 500 drops nearly 2%
Federal review blames leadership failures for Grand Canyon's Dragon Bravo fire destroying historic lodge
Handwritten draft of Martin Luther King Jr.'s 'I Have a Dream' speech on display in Atlanta before auction
AAA says high airfares and gas prices will keep some Americans from Thanksgiving travel
